_note: P1-T08. Thirty lines of regime voice. No audio assets: the game ships as one HTML file with no network, so 'audio' is text the player hears in their head plus a loudspeaker you can read. When real audio exists, these are the lines to record.
_rules: Never say: evil, hero, tyrant, freedom fighters, bad guys. The Directorate does not think of itself as any of those.
Bureaucratic register: passive voice, procedure as reassurance, 'we' meaning the building.
loudspeaker: The ration line opens in eleven minutes. Do not form more than one line.
Curfew pass checks are suspended for the morning period. They resume at 20:00.
Sector command reminds residents that silence is not evidence.
Anyone who has had their papers checked this week must have them checked again.
The east gate is closed to pedestrians. The east gate is not closed to authorised movement.
A child between the ages of six and fourteen must be accompanied at all times, and is not required anywhere.
radio: Kiln Row, this is Sector Four control. Mount your patrol.
Warden, compliance is not an opinion. File what you saw.
Your quota has been counted. It is short.
Sector Four has a quiet street. The Directorate likes quiet streets. Continue.
A patrol that reports nothing is a patrol that noticed nothing.
Warden. You are being assessed on the basis of tonight, not this morning.
ambient: A tram stops two streets away. It does not start again.
Someone upstairs drags a chair across the floor, twice, and then stops as if caught.
A loudspeaker clearing its throat before it decides to say nothing.
Two men arguing in another language about a door.
A printer working through a long job, undisturbed.
The blue of a surveillance lamp moving across a wall as it pans.
witness: I did not see anything. I want to say we both did not see anything.
Do you need my name, or do you already have my name?
